policy.text: Only a space administrator may remove another member from that space. This policy does not prohibit a member leaving the space themselves.

questions.request: Check DeleteSpaceMember in this Memos revision against the independently supplied current policy. Explain the actual behavior, including whether an ordinary space member may remove a different member and whether visible administrator-removal and self-removal paths differ; compare the behavior with the policy, cite the controlling source, and preserve any decisive missing facts. Do not assume deployment middleware or undocumented role grants.

premises.text: The independently supplied current policy states: "Only a space administrator may remove another member from that space. This policy does not prohibit a member leaving the space themselves."
Deployment middleware must not be assumed.
Undocumented role grants must not be assumed.

observations.subject: DeleteSpaceMember entry path
observations.claim: The public RPC is DeleteSpaceMember, exposed at DELETE /api/v1/{name=spaces/*/members/*}; the Connect handler delegates to APIV1Service.DeleteSpaceMember, which delegates to the store.

observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: The store deletion API explicitly receives actorUserID, and rejects a deletion request missing a positive actor ID; the available controlling implementation evidence therefore binds authorization to an actor user ID, without establishing any deployment middleware behavior.

observations.subject: selected membership
observations.claim: The deletion object selects a space ID and user ID, and the store API passes that selected membership plus actorUserID to the driver.

observations.subject: cross-member authorization
observations.claim: In the PostgreSQL implementation, when actorUserID differs from the target user ID, the operation requires the actor's active membership in the selected space and role ADMIN; otherwise it returns ErrSpacePermissionDenied. Thus an ordinary USER member cannot remove a different member on this visible path.

observations.subject: self-removal authorization
observations.claim: The PostgreSQL implementation does not apply the cross-member ADMIN check when actorUserID equals the target user ID; the API contract also states that a member may delete their own membership to leave the space.

observations.subject: membership deletion effect
observations.claim: The service invokes Store.DeleteSpaceMember for the selected space member and maps deletion errors; the store driver contract defines the deletion effect over that selected membership.

observations.subject: last administrator protection
observations.claim: The PostgreSQL path separately prevents removal of the last active normal administrator by returning ErrLastSpaceAdmin; this is an additional effect guard, not an expansion of ordinary-member removal authority.

result.scope: usememos/memos@cb42e326ba9cc266a6a9570c53e0fe04c62793f4; inspected the DeleteSpaceMember API contract, Connect delegation, store contract, shared membership definitions, and the PostgreSQL DeleteSpaceMember implementation. No deployment middleware or undocumented role grants assumed. This is not a claim of all-repository coverage.

observations.subject: DeleteSpaceMember entry path
observations.claim: The public RPC is DeleteSpaceMember, exposed as DELETE /api/v1/{name=spaces/*/members/*}; the Connect handler delegates to APIV1Service.DeleteSpaceMember, which invokes Store.DeleteSpaceMember.

observations.subject: caller identity
observations.claim: The store deletion API takes an explicit actorUserID and rejects a missing or non-positive actor ID. The inspected source binds the authorization decision to that actor user ID; it does not establish deployment middleware behavior.

observations.subject: selected membership
observations.claim: The request selects a membership by space ID and target user ID; the deletion object carries SpaceID and UserID, and the store passes that selected membership together with actorUserID to the driver.

observations.subject: cross-member authorization
observations.object: selected space membership and active ADMIN role
observations.claim: In the inspected PostgreSQL implementation, when actorUserID differs from the target user ID, the actor must have an ACTIVE membership in the selected space with role ADMIN. A missing membership or any non-ADMIN role returns ErrSpacePermissionDenied. Therefore an ordinary USER member cannot remove a different member on this visible implementation path.

observations.subject: self-removal authorization
observations.claim: The inspected PostgreSQL implementation skips the cross-member ADMIN check when actorUserID equals the target user ID. The API contract expressly says a member may delete their own membership to leave the space. Self-removal and removal of another member therefore have different visible authorization branches.

observations.subject: membership deletion effect
observations.claim: After the service and store validation path, the operation delegates deletion of the selected space/user membership to the store driver; the effect is on that membership, not an unrelated resource.

observations.subject: last administrator protection
observations.claim: The inspected PostgreSQL implementation separately rejects removal of the last active normal administrator with ErrLastSpaceAdmin. This is an additional protection on an otherwise authorized deletion and does not grant ordinary USER members cross-member removal authority.

behavior.explanation: The inspected implementation conforms to the supplied policy on the visible PostgreSQL path: an administrator may remove another member, an ordinary USER member may not remove a different member, and self-removal is allowed subject to membership/target validity and the separate last-administrator safeguard. Conformance for the revision as deployed remains conditional because the selected database driver and any deployment-specific middleware were not verified.

branches.condition: actorUserID != target user ID and the actor is an active USER member of the selected space
branches.explanation: The PostgreSQL guard requires the actor's active role to be ADMIN; USER receives ErrSpacePermissionDenied.

branches.condition: actorUserID != target user ID, the actor has an active membership in the selected space, and that membership has role ADMIN
branches.explanation: The cross-member role guard is satisfied. The deletion can still be denied if the target is absent, the space is absent, inputs are invalid, or removing the target would remove the last active normal administrator.

branches.condition: actorUserID == target user ID and the selected active membership exists
branches.explanation: The cross-member ADMIN check is not applied on the self branch, and the API contract documents self-deletion as leaving the space. Other validity and last-administrator checks can still affect the result.

branches.condition: actorUserID == target user ID and the target is the last active normal ADMIN
branches.explanation: The inspected PostgreSQL implementation returns ErrLastSpaceAdmin when removal would leave no active normal administrator.

branches.condition: actorUserID != target user ID and the actor lacks an active membership in the selected space
branches.explanation: The cross-member branch requires an active membership and ADMIN role; absence of that membership is denied.

policyAssessment.explanation: For the inspected PostgreSQL source path, the independent policy is satisfied: only an active space ADMIN may remove another member, while self-removal is separately permitted. No undocumented role grant or middleware protection was used. Overall revision/deployment conformance is conditional because the non-PostgreSQL driver bodies and deployment selection were not verified.
